lockFileMaintenance.description: Re-resolves every pin at once, so the per-version minimumReleaseAge cooldown cannot apply. Monthly, and only merged after a human checks the release dates.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

poetry.description: pfSentinel does not use Poetry. Left on, this manager reads pyproject.toml a second time without the lockfiles and opens duplicate PRs that raise floors but never update requirements*.lock.

pip-compile.description: Owns pyproject.toml together with requirements.lock and requirements-dev.lock. Their headers must use --extra=dev and --output-file= (with '='); Renovate rejects the short or spaced forms and then manages neither lockfile.

packageRules.description: The root pyproject.toml belongs to pip-compile, which updates it together with requirements*.lock. pep621 would read it a second time and open duplicate PRs without lockfile changes. pep621 stays on for .dagger/pyproject.toml (uv.lock).
Group non-major Python runtime deps from pyproject.toml [project.dependencies]
Group non-major Python dev deps from [project.optional-dependencies]
Major Python bumps: extra cooldown + manual review (C-extension wheel risk for lxml/cryptography/paramiko)
GitHub Actions: pin to SHA + group minor/patch/digest
GitHub Actions major updates require manual review
Security-critical packages: ungroup, raise priority, keep cooldown
The Dagger CI module (.dagger/): group its non-major updates into one PR.

Python versions change by hand, everywhere: requires-python, the CI python-version pins and the Dagger module. A new Python needs wheels for lxml, cryptography and paramiko first, and an automatic requires-python >=3.15.0 bump already broke Dagger CI once.
